title: Brookmere Clinic VPC & On‑Prem Provisioning - call scratch
content:
Call: Brookmere Clinic - Infrastructure & Inference provisioning (45m)
Date: 2024-11-03
Attendees: Dr. N. Redding (Brookmere CTO), Selena Park (IT ops), Avery Chen (Redwood AE/owner), Marcus Patel (Redwood solutions), Leah Ortiz (Redwood infra), Omar Khan (Brookmere SRE contractor)

Quick summary:
- Brookmere is piloting a hybrid deployment: dedicated VPC in us-east1 with a small on-prem rack for local inference to reduce egress and meet data residency for PHI.
- Primary ask: a secure, auditable Private control plane (Redwood Private) with KMS-integrated key management, per-request audit logging, and a simple installer for the on-prem worker pool.
- Timeline: pilot ready for clinical trial integration (read-only triage assistant) by mid-Jan; production pilot by end of Q1 2025.

Context / business constraints:
- Healthcare org, must meet internal compliance checklist and support monthly audit exports.
- No external PHI leaves their VPC unless specifically approved; prefer model weights hosted within Brookmere network if possible.
- Limited on-prem hardware initially: 2x A40-equivalent GPUs, 64GB RAM/host, will scale in later phases.

Notes from technical discussion:
- Networking:
  - Brookmere will provide a transit VPC to connect on-prem to the Redwood control plane via a site-to-site VPN (IPSec) or AWS Direct Connect equivalent. They want mutual TLS between control plane and agent.
  - CIDR ranges: 10.10.0.0/16 internal — need to avoid overlap with Redwood dev ranges. Ask: can Redwood support an overlay NAT if conflict occurs?
  - Inbound rules: control plane initiates connections; they prefer minimizing inbound firewall openings.

- Identity & Secrets:
  - KMS: Brookmere uses a cloud KMS (HSM-backed) for keys; requirement: Redwood must support customer-managed keys for model encryption and TLS certs.
  - RBAC: they want per-team API keys and Azure AD SSO integration for account management.

- Data flows and residency:
  - PHI documents must be processed inside Brookmere network; initial plan is to run inference on on-prem workers for any PHI-labeled requests, otherwise route to cloud hosted model for non-PHI.
  - Cache policy: KV-prefix caching must not persist PHI outside on-prem. Need documented guarantees and audit hooks.

- Model & performance:
  - Workload: triage assistant (clinical note summarization + classification). Typical request sizes: 1-2k tokens input, expected output 150-400 tokens.
  - Expected qps: 3 sustained, 20 spikes per minute during shift changes. Batch sizing: prefer low latency (SLO 1500ms 95th for on-prem).
  - They asked about quantized model variants to run on A40s; solutions team suggested 4-bit quantization and mixed precision to fit 70B-ish open models.

- Observability & compliance:
  - Need per-request audit logs (request id, user id, model/version, timestamp, node id) exported to their SIEM weekly and available for ad-hoc queries.
  - Retention: default 90 days for production, pilot 30 days. Must support manual export in CSV/JSON for compliance audits.

Gotchas / red flags called out by Brookmere:
- Hardware constraints: only two GPUs on-prem — if model footprint > 40GB (FP16), we need to provide a smaller model or orchestrated routing to cloud fallback.
- Network latency: site-to-site VPN introduces variability — must validate SLO across typical egress times.
- KMS policy: their security team requires proof that keys never leave their HSM — need clear documentation of crypto flow.
- Audit scope: Brookmere's compliance requires log immutability; normal writable logs will not be acceptable without append-only export.

Open questions (from Redwood team):
1) Can we support enforced 'no cache export' flag for PHI-labeled requests so KV cache never writes to disk on cloud? (owner: Leah Ortiz)
2) Does the installer support bringing up a minimal control-plane proxy inside their VPC to reduce cross-tenant exposure? (owner: Marcus Patel)
3) What is the minimal model variant we can recommend to guarantee 1500ms 95th on A40 x2 (owner: Avery Chen)
4) Who owns the runbook for crypto attestations to their security team? Need sample language. (owner: Omar Khan to coordinate with Brookmere)

Immediate next steps / action items:
- (Marcus) Prepare a trimmed deploy plan showing two fallbacks: (A) on-prem runs quantized 70B-lite model; (B) cloud-hosted smaller 13B fallback. Include latency and token-cost estimates. Due: 2024-11-10.
- (Leah) Prototype a config flag in the agent to tag requests as "phi=true" and enforce local-only execution; create a short PoC repo snippet. Due: 2024-11-17.
- (Avery) Draft an architecture sketch + customer readout for Brookmere security (KMS flow, immutability options) and share Confluence link. Due: 2024-11-08.
- (Omar) Share Brookmere's internal audit template with Redwood to align export fields. Due: 2024-11-07.
- Schedule follow-up: 30m technical sync week of 2024-11-11 to review PoC progress and finalize minimal model recommendation.

Notes-to-self / internal reminders:
- Check existing Private installer docs for 'local-proxy' mode — if not present, add a small design spike.
- Create an internal eval to benchmark 4-bit quantized Llama-variant on A40 single card with 2-card sharding to estimate per-request latency with 2k token input.
- Clarify default log retention & immutability options in Redwood Console — add as checkbox in onboarding flow for healthcare customers.

Reference artifacts mentioned during call:
- Brookmere compliance sheet (Selena to share) -> attach to INF-4821
- Example KMS attestation language: confluence:crypto-attest-templates
- Local installer repo: github:private-deployments/installer#312 (linked above)

Tone / misc:
- Keep notes concise for handoff to solutions engineering. Brookmere is risk-averse; emphasize options that minimize PHI egress and provide concrete fallback plans.

End of scratch notes.
